standard_prerequisites.name: Prefixed tableau construction
standard_prerequisites.statement: A modal tableau works with prefixed signed formulas S A [sigma]; rules extend branches by appending conclusions, some rules stack conclusions, some branch, some modal rules introduce a new prefix sigma.n, others require a prefix already used on the branch.

standard_prerequisites.name: Open and closed branches
standard_prerequisites.statement: A branch is closed if it contains an explicit contradiction; a tableau construction extends open branches; the finite set Gamma supplies the initial assumptions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Branch completeness
standard_prerequisites.statement: A branch is complete when the four conditions of the delivered definition hold: stacking conclusions present, a branching conclusion present, at least one new-prefix conclusion present, and used-prefix conclusions present for every used prefix.

core_obligations: Setup (472-474): consider an open branch of a tableau for Gamma; the prefixed formulas on the branch to which a rule could be applied are finite in number.

Fair saturation pass (474-479): in some fixed order (say, top to bottom), for each of these prefixed formulas for which the completeness conditions (1)-(4) do not already hold, apply the rules that can be applied to it; when a rule application branches, apply the treatment at the tip of each resulting branch for all remaining prefixed formulas.

Termination and recursion (479-483): since the number of prefixed formulas and of used prefixes is finite, the pass produces finitely many (possibly branching) extensions of the original branch; apply the procedure to each and repeat; by construction no applicable rule is left untreated, so the construction terminates with every branch complete.

proof_roadmap.step: Fix an open branch and observe finitely many rule-eligible prefixed formulas.
Run one fair pass in a fixed order, treating every prefixed formula that violates conditions (1)-(4), propagating through branching tips.
Argue termination from finiteness, recurse on the resulting branches, and conclude every branch is complete.

The 13-line proof is a fair-saturation termination argument: take an open branch, enumerate the finitely many prefixed formulas to which a rule could apply, apply all applicable rules to each in a fixed order (propagating to branch tips after branching), then repeat on each resulting branch; termination and completeness follow from finiteness of prefixed formulas and used prefixes. The solver must reproduce the fairness discipline (no prefixed formula is left untreated) and the recursion over the branching tree; the argument is short but the termination reasoning must be stated exactly.
